The two findings below are a real unauthenticated info-disclosure on the public /readiness probe (same raw-error leak class the dispatcher is fixing in api-handlers, but here reachable without auth).

evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/health.rs:177-182 — check_database()'s Err arm sets DependencyHealth.error = Some(format!("Database connection failed: {}", e)), interpolating the raw sqlx::Error Display into the response body. The readiness handler (health.rs:291-342) puts this straight into HealthResponse.dependencies (L299,L337) and returns Json(response).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/main.rs:471 — `/readiness` is mounted at the Router root. The only middleware layer on the app is api_core::middleware::host_tenant_middleware (main.rs:567-570, host/tenant resolution — NOT authentication), and the handler signature is `readiness(State(state))` with no PortalPrincipal/RequestPrincipal extractor. reality-server is the PUBLIC portal API with no global auth layer, so /readiness is reachable UNAUTHENTICATED from the internet.

Impact: when the DB is unreachable, any anonymous caller hitting GET /readiness (HTTP 503) receives the raw sqlx::Error Display, which for connection/auth failures can expose the DB host:port, username, SQLSTATE, and backend error text (e.g. 'password authentication failed for user ...', 'connection refused to <host:port>'). Same leak class the dispatcher is already fixing for authenticated manager endpoints in api-handlers (signals/2026-11-07-api-handlers-tier1d.json code-review-api-handlers-rentals-raw-db-error-leak), but worse here because exposure is to unauthenticated public callers. Landable backend-only fix: log e via tracing::error! and set error to a generic stable string (e.g. "database unavailable"), keeping the Unhealthy status/503 for probes. Call path traced end-to-end (route -> handler -> response); reachability is certain, kept at medium because the exact leaked content depends on the sqlx error variant.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/health.rs:330-340 — the same unauthenticated /readiness response (see sibling finding; main.rs:471, no auth extractor/layer) also returns commit = GIT_COMMIT (L333), built_at = BUILT_AT (L334), version (L332), and cache_metrics (L338) carrying token/health cache hits, misses, evictions, hit-rate and token_cache size (health.rs:303-322). The handler doc comment (health.rs:284-290 / 'Operator dashboards') implies it was intended for operators, but nothing gates it.
backend/servers/reality-server/src/main.rs:473 — GET /metrics (metrics_endpoint, main.rs:582-584) is likewise mounted at the root with no auth, exposing the full Prometheus text to anonymous callers.

Impact: unauthenticated fingerprinting / information disclosure on the public portal — exact git commit SHA + build timestamp let an attacker map the deployed build to known CVEs, and the cache internals/sizes leak operational detail. Lower severity than the raw-DB-error leak (no secrets, no outage required) so scored +1. Fix options (one change covers both findings): either put /readiness + /metrics behind an operator auth/allowlist, or strip commit/built_at/cache_metrics (and the dependency error strings) from the publicly reachable readiness body.
